newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says GMO guidelines will avert U.S. trade war.
newsitem.headline: EU says GMO guidelines will avert U.S. trade war.

text.p: European Commission guidelines on labelling genetically modified human and animal food should avert trade problems with the United States, a European Commission spokesman said on Thursday.
The spokesman was commenting after the Commission on Wednesday approved three options for labelling products containing genetically modified organisms (GMOs).
Food containing GMOs must be labelled together with the GMO percentage. Food that "may contain" GMOs must also be labelled. But labelling of GMO-free food is optional.
"We don't see why it should create trade problems," the spokesman said, adding that that the segregation of GMO and conventional farm products would not be required.
The U.S. is strongly opposed to the segregation of GMO maize, soybeans and other crops because of the huge cost and because it claims that they do not endanger human health.

U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Gkickman warned earlier this month that Washington would not tolerate any attempt by the EU to impose segregation of GMO farm products and would complain to the World Trade Organisation if this happened.

EU Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler, sensitive to European consumer pressure, notably in his native Austria, had sought compulsory labelling of animal feed and seeds irrespective of the amount of GMOs it contained.
He also sought segregation of GMO and conventional products throughout the production cycle from seed to final product.
Although the guidelines required neither segregation nor full labelling, Fischler's aides said that his basic demands had been met.
Firstly, the production technology would be labelled.
Secondly, products would be labelled throughout the production chain.
Thirdly, consumers would be informed so that they could make a real choice between GMO and traditional products.
Human and animal food must be segregated if it is labelled "GMO-free," the aides added.
